title: CordataProvenanceRunFacet
description: What was declared, and what authorised it. Emitted as `cordata_provenance` on every run event, terminal or not. The point of the whole block is that an auditor can get from a published number back to the reviewed commit without asking anybody — and, through source_published_by and source_published_release, back to the application release that set the shape it read.

descriptor_path.description: Path of the descriptor this run executed, relative to the root of the work tree holding it. Outside a work tree — which is what a run from an installed copy looks like — relative to the parent of its domain directory instead, so the same descriptor is named the same way wherever it ran; a descriptor too shallow to have a domain directory carries its file name alone. Never absolute: that would name the host's filesystem layout rather than the descriptor, and descriptor_sha256 is what proves which bytes ran.

descriptor_sha256.description: Hash of the descriptor bytes as they were when the run started — not as the file looks today. Kept here rather than moved to a standard facet because none carries it: sourceCodeLocation names a commit, and a commit is not the bytes that ran. A rewritten history, an uncommitted edit or a file assembled by a deployment step all produce a commit that resolves and bytes that differ.

source_table.description: Fully qualified name of the source the run read.

source_schema_version.description: The catalog version the descriptor pinned, and therefore the shape the input actually had.

descriptor_git_commit.description: The commit that last touched the descriptor. Null outside a repository — absence of provenance is not the same as bad provenance, and a consumer reading null knows to ask. Also emitted as the standard sourceCodeLocation job facet's version since 0.2.8, for a consumer that does not know this facet; kept here as well because descriptor_git_commit_signed below judges it and must have it to point at, and the two are built from one lookup so they cannot disagree. The standard facet is absent on a run that can name no remote, so this is the field that always carries the commit when there is one.

descriptor_git_commit_signed.description: Whether that commit's signature verified against a trusted key (git's `%G?` returning G). A run whose provenance points at an unsigned commit is itself a finding. Absent whenever descriptor_git_commit is, because a verdict with no commit to attach it to reads as a finding where the truth is that no commit was found — a run from an installed copy, outside any checkout, looks exactly like that. Present whenever a commit is named, which dependentRequired states. No standard facet carries it: OpenLineage can say which commit ran and nothing says whether anybody authorised it, which is the field this project exists to argue for.

executor_version.description: Name and version of the executor that ran this.

source_published_by.description: The producer that published the source version this run read — an application or team name, as the catalog records it. Absent when the catalog records no producer for that version, which is what a Glue version written by a crawler, or by a job that set no parameters, looks like, and absent on a run that read nothing, such as one that died on schema drift. Absent rather than null on the wire, because the OpenLineage client omits a field it has no value for.

source_published_release.description: The release reference that published that version — a tag or a commit. Absent under the same conditions as source_published_by, and never carried forward from an earlier version.

step_params.description: Parameter values substituted into the declared steps, keyed by step id. Where a model version lives, which is usually the most audit-relevant fact about a scoring run.
